\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حمایت} \fa{کردن} (hemâyat kardan)}{حمایت کردن (hemâyat kardan)}]{\fa{حمایت} \fa{کردن} (hemâyat kardan) — to support, to back}

\label{lesson:FA-C505-hemayat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a stranger, then the Persian for each other.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حمایت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{حمایت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{hemâyat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to support, to back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{خانواده} \fa{ام} \fa{همیشه} \fa{از} \fa{من} \fa{حمایت} \fa{میکنند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khânevâde-am hamishe az man hemâyat mikonand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My family always supports me.
\end{quote}

\emph{az kasi hemâyat kardan}; \emph{hemâyat} 'protection, support' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hemâyat} comes from Arabic \emph{ḥimāya}, 'protection' (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hemâyat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hemâyat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a stranger, then the Persian for each other, then say \emph{hemâyat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرزنش} \fa{کردن} (sarzanesh kardan)}{سرزنش کردن (sarzanesh kardan)}]{\fa{سرزنش} \fa{کردن} (sarzanesh kardan) — to scold, to blame}

\label{lesson:FA-C505-sarzanesh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for each other, then the Persian for to support.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرزنش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{سرزنش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{sarzanesh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to scold, to blame\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادر} \fa{بچه} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{خاطر} \fa{دروغ} \fa{سرزنش} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mâdar bachche râ be khâter-e dorugh sarzanesh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The mother scolded the child for lying.
\end{quote}

\emph{sar} 'head' + \emph{zan} 'striking' + \emph{-esh}, then \emph{kardan}. The reason takes \emph{be khâter-e}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarzanesh} is built on native Persian parts: EtymDB takes it as \emph{sar}, 'head', \emph{zan}, the stem of \emph{zadan}, 'to hit', and the noun ending \emph{-esh} (EtymDB): striking on the head, in words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarzanesh kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sarzanesh kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for each other, then the Persian for to support, then say \emph{sarzanesh kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دلداری} \fa{دادن} (deldâri dâdan)}{دلداری دادن (deldâri dâdan)}]{\fa{دلداری} \fa{دادن} (deldâri dâdan) — to comfort, to console}

\label{lesson:FA-C505-deldari-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to support, then the Persian for to scold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دلداری} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{دلداری} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{deldâri dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to comfort, to console\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دوستم} \fa{بعد} \fa{از} \fa{امتحان} \fa{به} \fa{من} \fa{دلداری} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dustam ba'd az emtehân be man deldâri dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My friend comforted me after the exam.
\end{quote}

\emph{del} 'heart' + \emph{dâr} 'keeping' + \emph{-i}, then \emph{dâdan} 'to give'. The person comforted takes \emph{be}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{deldâri} is built on native Persian parts: \emph{del}, 'heart', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian (EtymDB), \emph{dâr}, the stem of \emph{dâshtan}, and \emph{-i}: keeping someone's heart up. \emph{dâdan}, 'to give', is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{deldâri dâdan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to support, then the Persian for to scold, then say \emph{deldâri dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بغل} \fa{کردن} (baghal kardan)}{بغل کردن (baghal kardan)}]{\fa{بغل} \fa{کردن} (baghal kardan) — to hug; to pick up (a child)}

\label{lesson:FA-C505-baghal-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to scold, then the Persian for to comfort.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بغل} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{بغل} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{baghal kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to hug; to pick up (a child)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدر} \fa{دخترش} \fa{را} \fa{بغل} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedar dokhtarash râ baghal kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The father hugged his daughter.
\end{quote}

\emph{baghal} 'armpit; side; embrace' + \emph{kardan}. \emph{baghal} alone also means 'beside': \emph{baghal-e man}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{baghal} means 'armpit, side, embrace', but EtymDB has no entry for it, and its origin is not settled. \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to scold, then the Persian for to comfort, then say \emph{baghal kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نوازش} \fa{کردن} (navâzesh kardan)}{نوازش کردن (navâzesh kardan)}]{\fa{نوازش} \fa{کردن} (navâzesh kardan) — to caress, to stroke}

\label{lesson:FA-C505-navazesh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to comfort, then the Persian for to hug.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نوازش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{نوازش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{navâzesh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to caress, to stroke\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{گربه} \fa{را} \fa{آرام} \fa{نوازش} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u gorbe râ ârâm navâzesh kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She stroked the cat gently.
\end{quote}

\emph{navâzesh} 'a caress', from the stem \emph{navâz-} of \emph{navâkhtan}, + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{navâzesh} is built on \emph{navâz-}, the present stem of the native verb \emph{navâkhtan}, 'to caress; to play music', with the noun ending \emph{-esh}. EtymDB has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
